intro: This question helps us find the best place for you to begin.

widget.instructions: Build the set from intervals: drag or type endpoints, toggle whether each is included, and add a second interval for the second part.

stem: Write the set {x ∈ ℝ : {{cond}}} as a union of intervals.

hints.text: “or” means a number is in the set if it satisfies either condition. Draw each part separately. Watch the test point light up wherever the condition holds.
The first part has no lower bound, so it starts at −∞.

open-closed-confusion.text: The endpoints are right, but check which are included. The ringed endpoint is the one to fix.

missing-piece.text: This set has two separate parts, joined by “or”. Add the missing interval.

extra-piece.text: This set has exactly two parts.

wrong-endpoints.text: Check each endpoint against the condition.

infinity-closed.text: ∞ can never be included. Use a round bracket next to it.

generic.text: Draw each part of the condition on the number line, then join them with ∪.

workedSolution.text: First part: x {{symA}} {{a}}, everything to the left of {{a}}.
Second part: {{b}} {{symB}} x ≤ {{c}}. Watch the test point move along the line.

open-closed-confusion.front: x ≤ 3 or x < 3: which bracket at 3?

missing-piece.front: How do you write “x < 1 or x > 4” as intervals?

generic.back: Union: a number is in the set if it is in either piece.

accessibility.altText: A number line from −10 to 12 with one interval you can move, resize, and add to.
accessibility.nonDragAlternative: Type the union in the answer box, or use From, To, included and ∞ in Precise controls.
